content.text: I changed one line in `solution/core.py`, and all 3 visible tests now pass. The bug was operand order in the binary operators (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, EQ, LT, GT). The code read `a, b = pop(), pop()`, so `a` got the top of the stack, which is the right-hand operand, and `b` got the left-hand one. That explains all three failures. `PUSH 1, PUSH 2, LT` worked out `2 < 1`, so it returned 0 instead of 1. `PUSH 1, PUSH 0, DIV` checked the wrong operand for zero, so it computed `0 // 1` without raising `VMZeroDivision`. And `SUB` in the countdown loop computed `1 - x` instead of `x - 1`, so the counter never reached zero and the loop hit the step limit. I changed the line to `b, a = pop(), pop()`, which matches how `SWAP` already pops, so every binary operator now computes `second_from_top OP top`.

result: I changed one line in `solution/core.py`, and all 3 visible tests now pass. The bug was operand order in the binary operators (ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV, MOD, EQ, LT, GT). The code read `a, b = pop(), pop()`, so `a` got the top of the stack, which is the right-hand operand, and `b` got the left-hand one. That explains all three failures. `PUSH 1, PUSH 2, LT` worked out `2 < 1`, so it returned 0 instead of 1. `PUSH 1, PUSH 0, DIV` checked the wrong operand for zero, so it computed `0 // 1` without raising `VMZeroDivision`. And `SUB` in the countdown loop computed `1 - x` instead of `x - 1`, so the counter never reached zero and the loop hit the step limit. I changed the line to `b, a = pop(), pop()`, which matches how `SWAP` already pops, so every binary operator now computes `second_from_top OP top`.
